analysis.title: Hedge Fund Deep Dive Chartbook Q3 2026
key_insights: The hedge fund composite was flat (0.0%) in Q3 2026. Bonds fell 2.5% and equities gained 1.6%. Year to date the composite is +8.3%, against bonds at -2.7% and equities at +10.7%.

Only three of eight master strategies gained in Q3: quant +5.8%, long biased +0.8% and macro +0.8%. Equity long/short (-3.7%), arbitrage, credit and event (each -0.6%) and multi-strategy (-0.5%) lost.
Quant led the quarter and the year (+13.4% YTD). The CTA sub-strategy gained from sustained trends in rates and energy. Quant CTA is +16.1% YTD, with +4.4% in September.

Equity long/short was the weakest strategy in Q3 at -3.7%. Reversals in crowded AI and technology positions, particularly in Asia, drove losses and forced deleveraging. Equity long/short is still +10.7% YTD.

Industry AUM was above $3.8 trillion ($3,842bn) in September 2026, slightly below the August 2026 peak. Industry P&L plus net flows totalled $379bn YTD ($293.1bn P&L and $234.3bn net flows are among the chart figures). Quant, multi-strategy and macro drew the largest net inflows.

Long biased was the only master strategy with net outflows YTD. These partly offset its strong positive P&L. Arbitrage, the smallest strategy by AUM, had combined P&L and net inflows of about 15% of starting AUM.

Quant multi-strategy is the sub-strategy with the largest inflows in both dollars and percent of AUM. Aurum notes that a gap between flows and rolling 12-month performance can show delayed allocation decisions.

The March 2026 US-Israel-Iran conflict and oil shock produced the weakest monthly returns in the last 12 months. The composite lost 2.6% in March, against -6.6% for equities and -3.1% for bonds. Markets rebounded on US-Iran ceasefire hopes, and the composite was positive in every month of Q2.

Dollar P&L in April was just under $130bn and more than recovered March's losses, with all strategies contributing. Over the 12 months, equity long/short was the largest source of dollar generation, with quant and long biased also substantial.

Alpha, beta and risk-free decomposition over 10 years: composite return is 40% risk-free, 32% beta and 28% alpha. Multi-strategy is 63% beta and 2% alpha. Macro is 60% alpha and quant 47% alpha. Arbitrage beta is -5%.

Strategy diversification: quant has a 5-year correlation of -0.64 with bonds and about zero (0.00) with the composite. Quant CTA, quant macro and arbitrage tail have negative betas to both equities and bonds. Long biased and event activist have equity betas of about 0.7.
Dispersion is wide inside strategies. Long biased and equity long/short have the widest spreads of fund returns, with strong funds pulling means above medians. Quant had the highest mean return YTD.

Sub-strategy leaders YTD are ELS-APAC +29.1%, Long-Commodities +28.2%, Quant CTA +16.1%, Quant Multi +14.2% and Quant EMN +13.2%. Laggards are Credit Muni -2.2% and Arb Tail -1.8%. Credit Muni fell 4.2% in September.
By fund size, funds with $5bn to $10bn AUM are the strongest performers YTD. Funds of all sizes lost in March 2026.

Alt UCITS returned +0.8% in Q3 against 0.0% for the composite. YTD alt UCITS is +6.8% against +8.3%. Over five years every master strategy composite shown beat its alt UCITS subset, with the widest gap in multi-strategy at 7.0% annualised.

Alt UCITS arbitrage (+5.6% YTD) is the only alt UCITS strategy shown to beat its master-strategy composite (+3.7%). Alt UCITS make up 7.9% of industry AUM ($302.4bn), with long biased the highest at 13.9%. Aurum cautions the universes overlap and are unmatched.

Terms: weighted average fees range from long biased at 0.88% management and 12.97% performance to quant multi-strategy at 2.47% and 25.65%. Multi-strategy averages 1.83% and 20.89%. Credit direct lending has the longest total redemption lag of the major groups at 207 days.
